evaluation_dimensions.name: Architecture
evaluation_dimensions.description: Technical stack, service decomposition (micro‑services vs monolith), deployment model (cloud‑native, containerized), and extensibility points. Sources include white‑papers and API reference diagrams [[DOC-101]].

evaluation_dimensions.name: Enterprise Latency / Throughput
evaluation_dimensions.description: Measured end‑to‑end request latency under typical enterprise workloads and sustained throughput (requests/sec, data processed per second). Benchmarks derived from third‑party performance labs and in‑house load tests [[DOC-102]].

evaluation_dimensions.name: Pricing Predictability
evaluation_dimensions.description: Clarity of pricing tiers, usage‑based vs flat‑rate components, hidden fees, and cost‑simulation tools. Analysis based on public pricing sheets and historical invoice samples [[DOC-103]].

evaluation_dimensions.name: Advertised vs. Actual SLA
evaluation_dimensions.description: Comparison of vendor‑published service‑level agreements (uptime, latency guarantees) with observed performance and any SLA breach reports from customer case studies [[DOC-104]].

evaluation_dimensions.name: On-Prem / Hybrid Readiness
evaluation_dimensions.description: Availability of on‑premises or hybrid deployment options, required hardware, orchestration support (Kubernetes, OpenShift), and data residency controls [[DOC-105]].

evaluation_dimensions.name: Customer Sentiment & Trust
evaluation_dimensions.description: Aggregate sentiment from developer forums, GitHub issues, third‑party review sites, and Net Promoter Score (NPS) trends. Sentiment scoring methodology follows the approach outlined in the market‑research guide [[DOC-106]].

actions: Create a matrix of required data fields per dimension.
Establish inclusion/exclusion rules for sources (e.g., only reviews with >10 votes).
Download Python and TypeScript SDK packages from official repos.
Catalog supported API versions, installation footprints, and example completeness.
Deploy each service in a controlled cloud region.

quotes.quote: CloudScale reduced our Groq and OpenAI token costs by 28% within the first month. However, documentation for custom Python middleware is sparse, and we experienced two 3-hour outages in Q2 where support disputed our 10x SLA credit claim citing upstream cloud network degradations.

The semantic cache hit rate hovers around 22% in production, which is lower than the advertised 40%. The UI dashboard is intuitive, but on-prem installation took four weeks instead of the promised 48 hours.

DataPulse is unrivaled for real-time latency. Our fleet routing agents query fresh sensor states in 6ms. Be careful with high-volume Kafka topics, however; overage fees doubled our invoice in month three before we configured filtering.
Reduced our MTTR from 45 minutes to 11 minutes for recurring database and pod connection incidents. The safety guardrails are solid—it has never accidentally executed an unsafe command in production.

Veloce caught three sophisticated indirect prompt injection attempts during our clinical pilot. The false positive rate on medical abbreviations is slightly annoying (around 4%), but their customer support helped tune custom bypass dictionaries quickly.

outages_and_incidents.description: Two separate three‑hour service outages occurred in Q2; the customer’s request for a 10× SLA credit was denied by support, who attributed the failures to upstream cloud network degradations.
On‑premises deployment took four weeks, far exceeding the vendor’s promised 48‑hour installation window, indicating a significant delivery delay.

praise_and_positive_outcomes.description: Achieved a 28 % reduction in Groq and OpenAI token costs within the first month of use.
Delivered sub‑10 ms query latency for real‑time sensor data, highlighting strong performance for latency‑sensitive workloads.
Mean time to recovery (MTTR) dropped from 45 minutes to 11 minutes for recurring database and pod connection incidents; safety guardrails prevented any unsafe command execution in production.
Successfully detected three sophisticated indirect prompt‑injection attempts during a clinical pilot, demonstrating effective security controls.

usability_and_friction_points.description: Documentation for building custom Python middleware is described as sparse, creating integration friction.
Observed semantic cache hit rate of 22 % versus the advertised 40 %, indicating a performance gap; lengthy on‑prem installation further hampers usability.
High‑volume Kafka topics triggered overage fees that doubled the invoice in month three until proper filtering was applied.
False‑positive rate of approximately 4 % on medical abbreviations is noted as annoying, though support was able to tune custom bypass dictionaries.
